title: Build speech-to-text applications · Level 3
slo: Identify the Azure Speech components needed to transcribe microphone or file audio.

exercises.question_text: What can the Speech-to-Text API process into text? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The API can process voice input from a microphone. Spoken audio is converted into text.
The API can process voice from an audio file. The file's spoken content becomes text.
Speech-to-text works from spoken audio input. A microphone and an audio file are two possible sources.
Converting written text into audio is speech synthesis. Speech-to-text converts spoken audio into written text.
options.better_fit: Choose this for text-to-speech, which vocalizes text.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would produce audio instead of the needed transcript.
feedback.instructional: Match the direction carefully: speech-to-text is audio to text, while text-to-speech is text to audio.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The Speech-to-Text API turns spoken microphone or file audio into text.

options.text: A platform for building AI apps and agents
options.rationale: Microsoft Foundry brings models, services, data, and related resources together. Developers use it to build, test, and deploy applications and agents.

options.text: A library that converts audio to text
options.error_type: Confuses Foundry with the Speech-to-Text SDK
options.rationale: A client library contains ready-made code for an application. Microsoft Foundry is the broader platform where developers work with resources and services.
options.better_fit: Choose this for the Speech-to-Text SDK, which helps an application convert spoken audio into written text.

feedback.intrinsic: You would look for transcription code in the wrong place.
feedback.instructional: Keep the levels separate: Foundry is the platform, while the SDK is ready-made code used in an application.

options.text: A service address for an Azure resource
options.rationale: A service address is called an endpoint. Foundry is a platform, not the address used to reach one resource.
options.better_fit: Choose this when defining an endpoint for an Azure Speech connection.

feedback.intrinsic: The connection details would still be missing.
feedback.instructional: An endpoint tells the application where to connect; Foundry provides the place to build and test work.

options.text: A credential for signing in to Azure Speech
options.rationale: A credential proves that a connection is authorized. A Foundry resource key is a credential, but Foundry itself is not.
options.better_fit: Choose this for a Foundry resource key used to authenticate to Azure Speech.

feedback.intrinsic: You would confuse a platform with the credential needed for access.
feedback.instructional: A key authenticates a connection. Microsoft Foundry brings services and resources together.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Microsoft Foundry is a platform for building, testing, and deploying applications and agents.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the following setup steps for microphone recognition.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Recognition could be started before the app knows how to connect or where audio comes from.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Configure Azure Speech and the microphone first, create SpeechRecognizer with both configurations, then start continuous recognition.

exercises.correct_answer: Create SpeechConfig Create AudioConfig Create SpeechRecognizer Start continuous recognition
exercises.explanation: SpeechRecognizer needs connection details and an audio source before it can be created. Continuous recognition begins only after the recognizer is ready.

exercises.question_text: An API is a credential used to authenticate to an Azure resource.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The connection setup would mix up its interface and its credential.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: An API is a set of rules and endpoints for using another application's functions or data. A resource key is the credential used to authenticate.

exercises.explanation: Correct! An API supports communication between applications; a credential authenticates access.

exercises.question_text: What is an endpoint in an Azure Speech app?

options.text: The service address used to connect
options.rationale: An endpoint is the address application code uses to connect to an Azure resource. It identifies where the connection goes.

options.text: The credential used to prove identity
options.error_type: Confuses endpoint with a resource key
options.rationale: A credential authenticates the connection. An endpoint is the service address, not the proof of authorization.
options.better_fit: Choose this for a Foundry resource key or Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would know where to connect but not how to authenticate.
feedback.instructional: Separate address from authorization: the endpoint is the address, while a key or Microsoft Entra ID authenticates.

options.rationale: SpeechRecognizer is the object that performs transcription. An endpoint is connection information supplied to SpeechConfig.
options.better_fit: Choose this for SpeechRecognizer when identifying the object that transcribes audio.

feedback.intrinsic: The transcription object would still be missing.
feedback.instructional: SpeechRecognizer does the transcription. The endpoint only tells the application where the Azure resource is reached.

options.rationale: AudioConfig specifies an audio input or output source. An endpoint is the address of the Azure resource.
options.better_fit: Choose this for AudioConfig when selecting microphone or other audio input.

feedback.intrinsic: The application would have an audio source but no service address.
feedback.instructional: AudioConfig identifies the audio source. The endpoint identifies where the application connects.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The endpoint is the address application code uses to reach the Azure resource.

exercises.question_text: Which jobs can the Speech-to-Text SDK handle? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The SDK handles audio streaming between the application and Azure Speech. This supports sending audio for transcription.
The SDK handles response parsing. This helps the application receive transcription results.
The SDK handles networking and authentication. These tasks support a secure connection to Azure Speech.

options.error_type: Confuses SDK transport tasks with agent reasoning
options.rationale: The SDK handles connection and data-transfer work. Processing or reasoning about text belongs to application logic or an agent.
options.better_fit: Choose this for the processing stage that analyzes text or decides what to say next.

feedback.intrinsic: The application would assign a response decision to the wrong layer.
feedback.instructional: The SDK manages networking, authentication, streaming, and parsing. Reasoning happens after speech has been converted to text.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The SDK manages audio transfer, connection work, and handling returned results.

exercises.question_text: During continuous recognition, the event that returns completed text is the ___ event.

parts.text: During continuous recognition, the event that returns completed text is the

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An unfinished transcription could be treated as the completed result.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use recognized for completed text. Recognizing means interim text, while SpeechConfig handles endpoint and authentication details.

exercises.explanation: Completed text is returned by a recognized event. Recognizing events return interim text, and SpeechConfig supplies connection information rather than transcription results.

options.rationale: The SDK is a client library, meaning ready-made code. It helps an application communicate with Azure Speech and convert spoken audio into written text.

options.text: A portal for testing speech services
options.error_type: Confuses SDK with the Foundry playground
options.rationale: A portal playground is used to experiment with speech capabilities. The SDK is code used when adding transcription to an application.
options.better_fit: Choose this for the Speech-to-Text playground in Microsoft Foundry.

feedback.intrinsic: You would open a testing area instead of adding transcription code.
feedback.instructional: The playground is for experiments. The SDK is the client library used by an application.

options.text: A service address for Azure Speech
options.rationale: A service address is an endpoint. The SDK is a client library that communicates with the service.
options.better_fit: Choose this when identifying the endpoint used to connect to an Azure resource.

feedback.intrinsic: The application would have an address but no ready-made transcription library.
feedback.instructional: An endpoint tells code where to connect. The SDK helps the code make that connection and handle transcription.

options.text: A voice used to read text aloud
options.rationale: A synthetic voice is used for text-to-speech. The Speech-to-Text SDK handles spoken audio becoming written text.
options.better_fit: Choose this for a text-to-speech application that vocalizes written content.

feedback.intrinsic: The application would speak text rather than write down speech.
feedback.instructional: The Speech-to-Text SDK is for transcription. Voices belong to speech synthesis.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The Speech-to-Text SDK is client-library code that supports transcription in an application.

exercises.question_text: The Speech-to-Text SDK is used only after a completed transcription and cannot send audio.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The app would have no way to provide its microphone, file, or stream audio for transcription.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The SDK can capture or send audio securely to Azure Speech, then return transcription in near real time or after processing.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The SDK can capture or send audio before transcription results are returned.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the following steps for testing an uploaded recording in the playground.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: You could try to review a result before providing any recording.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start in the playground, provide the audio, let Azure Speech transcribe it, and then review the returned text.

exercises.correct_answer: Open the playground Upload an audio file Azure Speech transcribes Review the text
exercises.explanation: The audio must be available before transcription can occur. Reviewing comes last because the transcription is the result of processing the audio.

exercises.question_text: The Azure Speech ___ processes microphone or audio-file voice input into text.

parts.text: processes microphone or audio-file voice input into text.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The requested audio would not be matched to the transcription service.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use the Speech-to-Text API for voice input becoming text. Text-to-Speech and SpeechSynthesizer produce audio, while SpeechRecognizer is an application object.

exercises.explanation: The Speech-to-Text API processes spoken input from a microphone or audio file and returns text. Text-to-speech components work in the opposite direction, and SpeechRecognizer is the code object that performs transcription.

exercises.question_text: Which items can initialize the Speech SDK for an Azure Speech connection? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: An endpoint is the service address used to connect to an Azure resource. It is provided when the Speech SDK is initialized.
A Foundry resource key is a credential used with the endpoint. It authenticates the connection to Azure Speech.
Microsoft Entra ID is an alternative identity-based authentication method. It can be used when initializing the Speech SDK.

options.error_type: Confuses authentication setup with transcription results
options.rationale: A recognized event returns completed transcription text. It does not provide an endpoint or authenticate a connection.
options.better_fit: Choose this when responding to completed text during speech recognition.

feedback.intrinsic: The connection could not be initialized from a transcription result.
feedback.instructional: Initialize with a service endpoint and authentication, such as a key or Microsoft Entra ID. Recognized is an event after recognition occurs.

exercises.explanation: Correct! An Azure Speech connection needs an endpoint and authentication through a key or Microsoft Entra ID.
